independent.summary: The two tests that claim to pin id ordering are vacuous: each fixture workspace holds exactly one relationshipGroup and one openQuestion (so `deepEqual(ids, [...ids].sort())` compares a one-element array to itself), and alice's `entry_ids` were inserted Zephyr-then-Aleph, i.e. already in ascending ObjectId order — so deleting `.sort(cmpString)` from `asIdSet` and `.sort(byId)` from the exporter leaves the whole suite green, contradicting the file's own falsification claim that dropping any `.sort(…)` turns a test red. (Same cluster: `'members.userId'` in FORBIDDEN_KEYS can never be a key name returned by `allKeys`, so that sweep entry asserts nothing.)

grades.reason: `body` is read only through optional chaining (`body?.error`), so a null body yields `undefined` and falls back to `${res.status} ${res.statusText}` — no TypeError is possible.
The Decision Log line it cites explicitly states the filename is `<workspace>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.json` from an ASCII slug, with the Hebrew/Japanese fallback to `workspace` and the RFC 6266 follow-up named.

The interpolated value is `workspaceSlug(...)` output, which collapses everything outside `[a-z0-9]` to `-`, so quotes, `;`, CR/LF and `/` cannot reach the header — and `graphExporter.test.js` pins exactly those inputs.

Byte-identity is pinned where the item assigns it, in `tests/unit/graphExporter.test.js` ('two exports with the same timestamp are byte-identical'); the HTTP suite never claims to test it, and `exportedAt` is injected precisely so it can be.
The file contains `test('entity types sort by \`order\`, then name — not by insertion')` asserting `['Characters', 'Worlds']` against a fixture inserted Worlds-first.

The byte-identity test passes the same `EXPORTED_AT` to both exports, and a separate test compares two different timestamps only after deleting `exportedAt` from both — the stated scenario is not what the code does.

triageGrades.reason: The change adds a new route mounted behind `requireAuth` + `resolveWorkspace` in app.js and tests the 401/tenant-isolation behaviour, so the auth surface is touched.
No credentials or secret handling is added; `EXPORT_LOG_LEVEL` is a log knob, and the exporter deliberately excludes `passwordHash`/account fields.
`aiBudget` only appears as an excluded/forbidden key; no billing or spend logic changes.
The exporter and route are read-only (`find`/`findById` plus a response); nothing is written or deleted.
No third-party service is called — the only new fetch is the client calling this app's own `/export`.
No version bumps, deploy config, or packaging changes; `EXPORT_VERSION` is a document schema tag inside the app.
